title: Last universal common ancestor (LUCA)
summary: The last universal common ancestor (LUCA) was the theoretical ancestral organism from which all cellular life on Earth descended. Genomic and molecular clock analyses date LUCA to approximately 4.2 billion years ago during the Hadean eon, reconstructing it as an anaerobic acetogenic prokaryote possessing primitive viral defense mechanisms. Its early existence demonstrates that a complex microbial ecosystem emerged very rapidly after Earth formed.

uncertainty.note: Age estimate from 2024 cross-braced molecular clock analysis by Moody et al. in Nature Ecology & Evolution (95% confidence interval 4.09–4.33 Ga, centered at ~4.2 Ga).

where.modern_name: Global early Earth oceans and hydrothermal systems (no single preserved site)

paleo.not_applicable: Predates plate reconstructions; global biological ancestor.

importance.justification: The theoretical biological root of all cellular life on Earth, defining the transition from prebiotic chemistry to an integrated microbial biosphere.
